body:
## Description

Members previously showed pending invitations in a permanent card without a count. UI-04 uses a native **Pending invitations · N** disclosure: zero starts closed, nonzero starts open, and compact rows keep role, absolute UTC expiry and permitted Resend/Revoke actions. The same approved removal help follows the pending section; keyboard use, narrow screens and 200% text work with JavaScript on or off.

Stacked on [UI-03 #266](https://github.com/tomer-mayara/Thermus/pull/266). UI-02 #264 remains a sibling and is not included.

## Review

**T1 Team review — Architecture: T0: no architecture fact.** T1 comes from the updated `docs/implementation/test-gate-policy.md` read path.

**Architecture facts** (candidate `3380afe6` vs parent `12d1a3c5`):

- None.

Why, from `.pr-impact.json`: presentation stays in Web and uses the existing complete pending projection. Protected fields, allowed actions, authorization, provider operations, fixed outcomes and approved help bytes remain. All classification flags are false. Production architecture is unchanged; all 15 registry views remain accurate and all 49 public declaration snapshots are unchanged.

**Merge status: blocked; Draft.** Local functional and container checks pass. The required staging run passed 22/29: six cases share WorkOS’s sandbox invitation-email quota error; the scoped removal journey separately received HTTP 503 when reinviting a removed user. That response does not establish its provider cause. Both invitation paths must pass the required group before Ready. Independent authorized owner/team approval covering this exact head and scope is also required before merge. No merge or deployment is included.

---

Browser computed-style calls operate on attached Playwright documents, a button selected inside the pending details and the required Members heading. A missing window/ancestor/heading throws; the heading must then measure 64px after explicit resize. The independent reviewer checked each. Extra guards could improve diagnostics but add no missing behavior check.

Retained comments preserve these limits: WorkOS composition/fake-role assumptions, product-seat fixtures, CSRF retrieval and reads versus writes in hosted-workos-administration; the complete-read precondition in administration-pages; Origin omission, raw duplicate fields, cookie/redirect boundaries, loopback Host semantics, accessible form names and token-safe diagnostics in hosted-browser; the narrow email/role projection in pending-invitations-page; and safe reports, boolean-only secret checks, session lifetime, actual form submission and private invitation credentials in hosted-live administration-server.

The four long files remain cohesive: live administration owns a scoped provider journey; the browser runtime keeps fresh Members/invitation/removal/Audit cases with mechanics in separate drivers; WorkOS administration keeps its role/refusal matrix and assumptions; page integration keeps the public page's count, scope, actions and escaping contract. Generic scenario plumbing or arbitrary file splits would hide those checks.

</details>
